summary.en: Restore more Pokemon and create custom gifts in Sword and Shield, edit DLC encounters and material drops in Scarlet and Violet, and follow individual files during Apply. KM Editor 2.6.9 also reorganizes the main editors and expands the Sword and Shield Randomizer.

body.en: Restore 247 additional regular species and forms, including Primal forms, and 91 Mega forms. The catalog now has 298 regular entries and 91 Mega entries, all marked In testing. Use your own compatible donor files to prepare models, animations, cries, party sprites, and gameplay records.

Create code gifts and badge based reward pools with Royal Gift and Mystery Gift. Royal Gift has its own menu name and icon. Gift codes accept all uppercase letters and digits, and Royal Candy has its own crowned icon.

Use Update Asset to bring supported Pokemon installed outside KM Editor under editor management. Review the affected files before applying, with compatible customizations and assignments preserved. Restoration progress identifies the assets being converted.

Wild Encounters shows named forms and updates the sprite as you change species or form. Wild held items appear with the selected Pokemon's other settings and are shared across encounters for that species and form.
Randomizer adds options for trainers, shops, world items, and more, with settings grouped by what they affect. KM1 seeds still reproduce the selected result against compatible starting data.
Disable Poke Jobs at the terminal or disable Y Comm while retaining access to Mystery Gift. Shared executable edits for Shaking Trees are recognized when they are already installed.
Restored Pokemon have improved Summary framing, battle transitions, and party sprites. Preparation reuses identical texture images, and supported expanded tables receive the memory changes they need.
Edit Kitakami and Blueberry Academy wild encounters alongside Paldea. Region labels also identify the new tables in game dumps.
Edit a Pokemon's material item and count, or use Material Drop Count to set a shared count for every Pokemon with an active material drop. Pokemon without a material keep their empty drop.

Move descriptions match their game text entries, including moves after Tera Blast. The IV and EV Summary views restore radar graphs and display numeric values, and TM recipes and tracking show undiscovered material names.
Pokemon gender categories and ratios save using the game's native values while preserving settings for other forms.
Pokemon, Trainer, Item, and Move editors group related fields into compact sections. Drafts remain available when you switch sections.
Apply shows the active step, elapsed time, and the files being staged or written. The reviewed file list remains available while Apply runs.
Copy and paste complete learnsets between compatible Pokemon records. Learnsets stay in level order, and learnset and evolution edits remain local until Stage.
Project Setup gives Project Paths the full width of the page. Validation, diagnostics, and cache status remain available.
Update desktop dependencies for TLS, certificate validation, and XML parsing. App updates continue to use the signed installer.

summary.en: Restore the Geodude and Alolan Geodude families in Sword and Shield, add omniboosts to ordinary moves, and work with clearer Legends Arceus records. KM Editor 2.6.8 also improves editor loading, memory use, recovery, and reviewed saves while removing Analysis Tools.

body.en: Restore Geodude, Graveler, Golem, and their Alolan forms as six independent entries from your own compatible S/V donor files. The catalog now offers 51 supported species and form entries, all marked In testing. Regional typings, evolution targets, cries, icons, and supported model effects retain their separate identities.

Add omniboosts to ordinary moves with All Stats, which raises Attack, Defense, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def, and Speed by the configured amount and chance. Use Damage + User Stat Raise for a damaging move's secondary boost. The existing All Stats (move specific) option retains its scripted meaning, and normal move conditions still apply.

The 60FPS Patch corrects stadium screen animation timing and prevents the reproduced Gigantamax appearance stall. Reapply the configuration to update existing output. Verified pasted FPS updates can also be removed and reapplied while preserving unrelated files and edits.

Update Asset appears only when a newer revision is available for that restored Pokemon. Large valid restoration collections remain available for editing and assignment, and removal releases unused prepared assets when Apply finishes while retaining resources needed by recovery.

Game Options changes no longer report an unchanged review as stale after Pokemon restoration. Trainer species replacements use the matching reviewed roster header, including modified parties whose size stays the same. Changes made after Review and inconsistent rosters remain blocked.

Invalid held item slots encoded as -1 display as None and receive ordinary pending corrections after a successful stage in the Pokemon editor. Opening the editor does not change output, and explicit valid item choices take priority.

Sound Studio names and filters complete supported restored cry sets in copied output even without restoration ownership metadata. Recognition preserves the audio files and does not adopt ownership of the restoration.

Placement avoids rebuilding shared field definitions and repeating item choices on every visible row, reducing loading work and oversized responses while preserving individual choices and protected fields.
Encounter restoration and scripted boss catalogs reuse shared identity and selector lookups. Missing or ambiguous records and unsupported boss combinations retain their existing protections.

Trainer names, classes, Pokemon forms, encounter regions, outbreak summaries, research requirements, and Ginkgo offers use clearer descriptions and the appropriate game text. Trainer searches keep parties together, and protected selectors show their names without allowing unsupported replacement.

Field help explains inherited encounter levels, relative weights, effort values, move styles, action order, research thresholds, and event settings in all seven interface languages. Shop drafts and pending changes reflect the selected inventory, and move records distinguish partial editing from protected data.

Opening editors, preparing caches, reviewing changes, and refreshing after Apply avoid repeated source loading and validation. Model, texture, voice bank, executable, and script inspection use fewer temporary allocations while retaining source checks and output preservation.

Completed vanilla cache preparation remains ready after output changes. Minimal, Balanced, and Performance modes, the 2 GB cache limit, interrupted write recovery, and checks for actual source changes remain in place.

Analysis Tools, including Balance Lab, Guided Design, Semantic Merge, Game Modules, Research Lab, and standalone Semantic Explore, have been removed. Record search, Inspector, bookmarks, notes, saved views, output profiles, and game data caches remain available.
Compact progress cards keep elapsed time beside the steps and animate only the active phase. Cancellation, errors, final outcomes, accessibility, and reduced motion remain supported.

Routine interface updates preserve loaded recovery status, History, Checkpoints, and active checkpoint write guards. Closing the app or changing projects cancels disposable reads while active Apply and protected operations finish at their safe boundaries.
Update Zod to address memory exhaustion when validating oversized constrained collections, and update Vite to address development server and editor integration vulnerabilities.

summary.en: Bring your ideas to Hisui with Legends Arceus editors, restore 33 more Pokemon in Sword and Shield, and customize Scarlet and Violet's Summary views and Tera Blast. KM Editor 2.6.7 also adds restoration updates that preserve assignments, global held item chances, and clearer progress in the editor and Windows setup.

body.en: Restore 33 more missing Pokemon, bringing the supported total to 45. The complete Johto, Sinnoh, Unova, and Kalos starter families are now available, with each Pokemon selected independently from your own compatible S/V or Z-A donor files.

Update Asset refreshes an existing restoration without removing it from encounters, trainers, or other editor assignments. Updated defaults replace unchanged stats and learnsets, while supported customizations remain intact. Conflicting model edits stop the update rather than being silently discarded.

Restoration preparation improves texture detail, material shading, battle idle behavior, static party artwork, and species specific eyes, flames, and framing. The conversions remain Testing. Froakie can briefly show blank eyes during battle entry before returning to normal.

Restoring or updating Pokemon also installs the required sound memory changes for Sword and Shield 1.3.2. Copied restoration output and its model dependencies are handled more reliably during reviewed Apply. Disable older standalone sound memory patches when using the integrated restoration output.

Set global normal and boosted held item percentages for all three slots. Stage global chances replaces existing individual chances without changing held items, and you can customize individual Pokemon again afterward, including before Apply.

Restore Missing Pokemon includes a saved PLA donor folder for future sources and lists 122 additional form candidates. Those form entries are not installable, and the folder does not add a PLA conversion adapter.

Search Shaking Trees by eligible drop item names. Trainer Whiteout now enters forced defeat recovery before battle scenes resume, and 60FPS output includes corrected field crowd animation with support for complete output transactions.

Add four Summary views with the Beta IV and EV Screen: calculated stats, raw IVs, numeric EVs, and the original EV graph. The existing graph control cycles between views without changing Pokemon or save data. Raw IVs do not include Hyper Training adjustments.

Tune seven Tera Blast settings in Moves, including type and category behavior, Stellar power, effectiveness, and Attack and Sp. Atk drops. Battle previews follow the settings, and ordinary move data and executable changes apply together through the supported output modes.

Open Legends Arceus 1.1.1 projects with dedicated Pokemon, Moves, and Text editors. Edit personal data, learnsets and mastery, supported evolutions, and move tutoring through the shared Stage, Review, Apply, and History workflow.

Edit supported trainer teams and the available gift and static encounter fields while preserving scripted roles and protected event conditions. Familiar Pokemon layouts, contextual form choices, bulk experience changes, typed row clipboard actions, tabs, and bookmarks carry over to the new editors.

Edit Items, Crafting, Shops, Ginkgo inventory, Pokemon Drops, Research tasks, and rank requirements. Gameplay Rules includes capture factors, friendship changes, shiny bonus rolls, all 39 bag expansion prices, and 14 charm price controls.

Adjust existing wild encounter slots, supported Alpha traits, spawn counts, outbreaks, massive outbreaks, space time distortion encounters and items, and area weather weights. Shared tables affect every linked consumer, while protected story conditions and resource links remain intact.

Use the familiar Type Chart grid while retaining PLA's combined damage rules. Preview Pokemon models and animations, edit supported materials and color textures, and browse recordings in Sound Studio. Audio replacement, general script editing, complete starter replacement, and unsupported model authoring are not included.

Choose Minimal, Balanced, or Performance Data Cache modes with optional background preparation. Loose table editors work without the compression runtime; archive editors and selected model preparation require compatible Oodle support. PLA writes standalone output, with game specific source checks and preservation. Analysis Tools are unavailable for PLA and remain separate from its supported editor data cache.

More editor operations report their actual activity and measured progress. Windows setup shows current installation, repair, or uninstall work, including available file and byte progress, elapsed time, and the age of the last update.
CSV, TSV, and TXT exports identify their UTF-8 encoding, and Sword and Shield rental exports include all named moves. Desktop build checks close their temporary watchers cleanly.

Reviewed output better preserves supported copied installations and independent editor changes. Deleted generated output can be recreated from valid current sources without replaying old History entries. Existing Gameplay Settings packages still need Refresh and Upgrade after relevant standalone changes.

summary.en: Bring missing Pokemon back to Sword and Shield, explore with outdoor camera controls, and build your own training and reward progression. KM Editor 2.6.6 also adds clearer progress feedback, customizable editor categories, faster restoration output, and a new home for the community on Discord.

body.en: Bring twelve missing Pokemon back under their original species IDs with Restore Missing Pokemon. Prepare and enable Ekans, Arbok, Weedle, Kakuna, Beedrill, Pidgey, Pidgeotto, Pidgeot, Kecleon, Piplup, Prinplup, and Empoleon individually from your own compatible S/V or Z-A donor files. Each conversion remains marked Testing.

Explore supported outdoor maps with Camera Control and its in game Unlocked Camera choice. The added camera yields to events and indoor areas, with extended scenery and NPC visibility while active. Camera Hook handles emulator settings separately from game output. Camera Control remains a Beta feature.

Offer Hyper Training at Pokemon Centers before Champion status, choose its minimum level, and customize both payment items. Service dialogue and party picker eligibility stay in step. IV Screen now shows 31 for Hyper Trained stats and raw IVs for untrained stats, including the training panel and its graph.

Shape berry tree rewards and encounters with Shaking Trees. Edit 73 ordinary item pools, 33 shared encounter areas, risk and loss rules, and supported quantities from one through three, with probability previews before staging.

Set traded Pokemon obedience limits independently for every badge count with Obedience Level. Battle Items adds a separate Beta restriction for ordinary player Bag items, preserving native ball rules. Installed camera and battle choices can also be configured through Game Options.

Starter replacements synchronize their supported scenes, cries, names, and dialogue. Restore an individual gift to its original record, synchronize earlier starter edits, edit received trade nicknames, and keep trade dialogue or the Wedgehurst station scene aligned with supported Pokemon replacements.

Restored Pokemon integrate with supported data, encounter, team, model, and audio tools. Conversions include normal and shiny resources, supported animations and facial channels, cries, native sized party icons, and ordinary Dynamax assets. Unsupported moves are omitted; unsupported abilities use an eligible ability from that same donor species and form.

Preparation remembers donor and Oodle folders, reuses compatible donor caches, and starts a temporary session cache when needed. Prepared entries offer Remove Assets through Stage, Review, and Apply, including tracked model customizations. Dependent references must be cleared, while unrelated output and recovery checkpoints remain protected.
Tune Blueberry Quest BP rewards and Support Board prices with dedicated editors, including filtered bulk changes and scoped Restore Vanilla actions.

Choose solo and group quest eligibility separately for each edition in Snacksworth, or make all treats available through solo quests. Supported dialogue follows those choices while later custom Text edits and player progression remain preserved.

Shared output composition better preserves independent Text, TM, Titan, and other supported editor changes. Separately installed Gameplay Settings packages still need Refresh and Upgrade after standalone edits.

Shared native output preparation preserves current descriptor and Text contributions when combined with supported standalone edits. The separate Z-A donor pipeline also supplies compatible source assets for the supported Sword and Shield restorations.

Long operations now show their current activity, elapsed time, measured counts, and workflow stages in a consistent progress card. Loading, asset preparation, Review and Apply, imports, exports, models, audio, updates, and Mod Merger distinguish completion, failure, cancellation, and waiting without inventing progress percentages.

Arrange the editor around your workflow with custom categories, saved names, editor ordering, and category ordering. Restore Original Categories offers a confirmed reset, and distinct editor icons make the sidebar and workflow cards easier to scan.

Review and Apply reuse verified restoration assets within each operation and avoid repeated mixed plan construction. Current source checks, stale review rejection, rollback, and ownership validation remain in place.

The Welcome Hub links directly to KM Hub on Discord and includes a new developer message. Updated wiki guides explain the new tools and their limits, with contextual help links from the affected editors.

Shared editor output, selective restoration, and recovery better preserve independent changes in existing mod projects. Gift, trade, and rental table expansion retains alignment, while NPC gift review handles edits across multiple scripts.
Updated source map and TLS dependencies address the reported dependency vulnerabilities. The Windows setup, updater, and application metadata consistently identify version 2.6.6.

summary.en: KM Editor 2.6.5 adds editable YAML game dumps, Game Options and per Pokemon held item chances for Sword and Shield, and the Beta Titan Swapper for Scarlet and Violet. It also adds trainer AI flag repair and Mum's starting money, improves custom model previews, and fixes cache reuse, scrolling input and trainer controls.

body.en: Game Dump exports readable, editable YAML for every available category across all five games. Named fields and nested records separate editable values from reference information, and large categories split into numbered files at record boundaries.

Dump Importer accepts YAML through the existing editor validators. Invalid entries identify the file, line, column and field while preserving the previous pending session. Valid reimports replace their own prior batch and retain unrelated edits. Existing CSV, TSV and JSON item price imports remain available.
Prepared caches are reused after projects reopen. Missing, changed or invalid entries are verified or rebuilt while current output remains separate from reusable base data.
Trainer search matches the name displayed in the trainer table. Party Pokemon, moves and source metadata no longer produce unrelated results.

Game Options sets starting values and hides individual selections for all 16 stock options in version 1.3.2. On takes priority over Default; Off excludes a starting choice but leaves it available to players. Hide removes that choice from navigation. Existing saves retain visible player choices, while hidden saved values fall back to the configured start.

Held Item Chance provides three searchable item choices and separate normal and boosted percentages for each Pokemon and form. It uses the Pokemon editor's selector and search. Each rate group totals at most 100%, with the remainder and empty slots giving no item. Restoring default chances retains the selected items and other Pokemon's settings.

Custom held item rates apply literally even when the first two slots contain the same item. Pokemon without a custom override retain inherited rates and the original matching slot behavior. Explicit encounter items can still take priority. Refresh and upgrade an installed Gameplay Settings package after changing or restoring Held Item Chance or Game Options.

Fix AI Flags reviews possible legacy switching selections per trainer or as a batch. It stages the proposed Fire Gym Rival to Switch Pokemon correction through ordinary trainer editing, preserves other flags and unknown bits, and never changes records automatically on load. AI help explains the native script meanings and custom script limits.

NPC Item Gift includes Mum's starting pocket money with one Amount field from 0 through 9,999,999 and a default of 30,000. The event adds the amount when it runs; this does not directly change an existing save balance. Other supported script edits remain preserved.

The 60FPS Patch consumes each accepted list input once and retains queued directions through scrolling. Existing output needs the patch reapplied to receive the correction. Base prize money choices show calculated amounts using the last occupied trainer party slot's level x stored rate x 4. Necrozma, Dusk Mane and Dawn Wings retain distinct names and sprites.

Titan Swapper is a Beta Editor for version 4.0.0. Choose a separate battle Pokemon and level for each of eleven phases while retaining the original story actor. The roster includes Klawf, Bombirdier, Orthworm, the edition's Great Tusk or Iron Treads, Dondozo and final Tatsugiri. Full encounter behavior remains pending in game verification, and native Gameplay Options cannot be combined with this editor.

The five Titan partner teams synchronize supported base form lead changes with their scene actors. Terastallization is blocked for these teams because it can prevent the battle from progressing. Other partner teams keep their existing controls.

The next editor output can repair eligible older KM owned Titan and Arven edits, including when applying an unrelated edit. Current choices and externally modified files are preserved. Titan phase rows also accommodate longer text without overlapping labels.
Project reopening reuses prepared cache progress and supported payloads within the selected cache mode and limits. Invalid entries still fall back to their original sources.
Atomic cache publication retries brief Windows access and sharing failures. The previous complete cache file remains available until replacement succeeds; persistent failures still report normally.

Supported custom replacements in the existing game formats use their current geometry, materials, textures and animations for preview and editing. Original comparison and restoration resolve clean base dependencies separately, preserving unrelated resources.

Preview handles additional BGRA textures, stored mip tails, repeated node labels, incomplete preview triangles and BC7 edge blocks. Malformed or unsupported resources remain rejected rather than being rewritten to fit the preview.

Supported fire materials use their source colors, textures, linked masks and animation channels. Enabled emission maps retain their authored gain. Fire rendering remains approximate; these improvements do not add geometry, skeleton or animation authoring.

Editor guidance and diagnostics have improved translations across all seven interface languages. The welcome hub includes the 2.6.5 notes and a new developer message, with contextual help for Game Options, Held Item Chance, Fix AI Flags and Titan Swapper.
Application, setup, updater and window title metadata identify KM Editor 2.6.5 consistently.
The Windows release includes the custom x64 setup executable, its updater signature, the updater manifest and checksums.

summary.en: KM Editor 2.6.3 introduces Basic and Advanced mod merging with archive imports and optional package selection. It adds Legends Z-A Behavior and Alpha Size controls, Marnie Wyndon Boosts for Sword and Shield, clearer evolution and relearn moves, and fixes for editing performance, output compatibility and 60 FPS timing.

body.en: Combine mod folders and ZIP, RAR or 7z archives for all five games. Basic compares the supplied mods without an original game dump; Advanced uses matching original files to combine independent edits while separating them from unchanged data. Mod Merger is available before project validation.

Sources containing multiple or optional packages open a separate selection dialog. Choose components, inspect their documentation, and manage the selection later. Author manifests can declare dependencies, required components and alternatives. A merge accepts up to 64 sources and 64 selected packages.

Supported game tables merge by record and field, with explicit choices for conflicting edits. Textures, audio, models and unsupported formats use complete file choices. Packed containers and descriptors retain their format specific restrictions; the merger does not assume arbitrary byte changes are compatible.

IPS, IPS32 and supported PCHTXT patches combine by executable address. Advanced can compare compatible executable images against matching originals. Related settings stay together, including Shiny Rate, Hyper Training and Marnie or Fairy Gym outcomes, while independent edits remain separate.

Review checks trainer identity, EV totals, encounter level bounds, linked party counts and dependent files. Z-A Behavior fields compose independently where supported. Changed inputs or unresolved conflicts require another review before export. Saved package choices, destination history and recovery remain available, and changing packages or output layouts removes only reviewed merger owned files.
Text staging reads the selected data without repeatedly loading unrelated archives. Repeated editing also releases obsolete workflow snapshots, reducing memory growth during long sessions.
Evolution moves display and accept level 0 across all five games. Native evolution markers are preserved when saving, and unrelated learnset fields remain unchanged.
Long Windows output paths remain editable after files are created. Repeated Apply, output history and checkpoint restoration retain their protections in deeply nested folders.

Item Data and Use Flags use the available editor width. Editor confirmations, pending labels and package guidance have improved translations across all seven interface languages, with more specific diagnostics for actionable failures.

Marnie Wyndon Boosts appears below Fairy Gym Boosts in Advanced Editors. Choose supported stat outcomes for both answers in each of the three Wyndon battles, stage the changes, and restore the original outcomes when needed.
Marnie and Fairy Gym outcome edits preserve installed 60FPS sequence timing. Applying or removing the timing patch preserves those outcomes and other compatible script edits.

60FPS timing now coordinates supported battle sequences, attack windup, cameras, field effects, script waits, movement, messages and menu repeat timing. Recognized older output can be upgraded while preserving unrelated edits. Unsupported cinematics can still require separate timing work.

Trainer Whiteout accepts compatible executable growth from other tools while retaining its build and instruction checks. Shared script editing preserves independent Raid Dens and other supported changes. Royal Candy customization preserves supported text and visual choices.
Text staging avoids repeated full archive scans, improving the first edit and subsequent changes. Other archive staging operations reuse a fresh source snapshot for the current operation.

Starmobile edits can be applied repeatedly under long output paths, including after generated output is deleted and recreated. Combined move assignments continue to validate against the final staged move data.

Behavior appears below Pokemon in Editors. Choose a wild temperament preset, adjust sight, hearing and home range fields, initialize missing wild tags, or restore the selected resource to vanilla. These controls do not guarantee roaming or attacks where encounter templates or other game systems are missing.

Pokemon includes Alpha Size controls with native scale multipliers, two decimal places for manual input, ordinary midpoint context and exact vanilla restoration. Shared form and gender resources are identified. Required size fields are added automatically for supported forms that did not enlarge by default.
Learnset rows show level 0 as Evolution. A Relearn checkbox identifies and sets reminder moves without requiring the internal level marker; mastery levels remain independent.
Behavior and ordinary Pokemon edits participate in shared Review and Apply across the supported output layouts. Restoring Behavior or Alpha Size preserves unrelated fields owned by other edits.
Tooltips dismiss correctly after pointer interaction while retaining keyboard focus behavior. Recent tabs and evolution sprites handle additional editing and navigation cases.
The welcome hub includes the 2.6.3 notes and updated developer message. Contextual help links lead to refreshed merger guides, Z-A Behavior and Marnie Wyndon Boosts documentation.
Application, setup, updater and window title metadata identify KM Editor 2.6.3 consistently.
The Windows release includes the custom x64 setup executable, its updater signature, the updater manifest and checksums.

summary.en: KM Editor 2.6.2 adds Trainer Whiteout, Trainer Dynamax and Raid Dens controls for Sword and Shield. It improves combined editor output, keeps editing available after generated files are deleted, stages Wild Encounter drafts together, and expands Legends Z-A TM numbering and compatibility editing.

body.en: Deleting generated output files or folders no longer prevents valid editing. Missing files fall back to vanilla, and Apply creates only the output required by the pending changes. Deleted saved edits are not replayed from History. Readable existing output and unrelated edits are preserved.

Combined editor sessions handle shared source files and dependent edits together. Pokemon data and trainer party changes can apply in one operation, and move changes are resolved before dependent Sword and Shield Rental Pokemon or Scarlet and Violet Starmobile edits. Invalid combined edits still prevent partial output.

Wild Encounter drafts across records and slots now use one Stage Encounter Changes action in every supported game. Copying, pasting and valid draft edits update slot names, sprites, levels and probabilities immediately. Failed staging preserves drafts, and successful staging preserves newer input.
A failed Apply retains pending edits and diagnostics, clears the obsolete reviewed plan, and leaves the progress indicator at Review. Correct the reported problem and review again before writing.

Trainer Whiteout is a new Beta editor with a searchable table of 436 trainer records, Yes and No choices, Reset to Vanilla, Enable Whiteout All and Disable Whiteout All. Select anywhere on a row, stage the desired settings, then review and apply through Changes. Disabling whiteout does not turn a defeat into a victory.

Trainer Whiteout writes the battle scripts and executable callbacks required by the selected trainer settings instead of rewriting every supported script. Shared scripts preserve compatible Raid Dens edits, and executable changes preserve FPS and other registered patch owners. Repeated uses of one trainer record share its setting; generated Battle Tower opponents are outside individual whiteout control.

Trainer Dynamax is a new Beta editor with independent Enabled and Disabled permissions for the player and opponent, per trainer reset and separate mass actions. Review and Apply stay inside the editor. All 436 roster records can be configured when used as opponents; repeated uses of one record share a setting, and generated Battle Tower battles use the mass settings.

Dynamax permission is separate from trainer team flags. Team Can Dynamax fields remain in Trainers, and the original Band, Pokemon eligibility and usage checks remain. Verified vanilla permissions are displayed where established; unknown original battle routes are labeled instead of assigned a guessed value. Enabling permission does not guarantee an opponent will choose Dynamax. Trainer Dynamax remains Beta.
Trainer Dynamax can apply, upgrade or remove its own executable patch while preserving Trainer Whiteout, FPS and other registered executable edits.

Raid Dens appears under Tools below Profanity Filter Bypass. Disable or restore the entire den interaction, including the den menu, starting a raid there, collecting Watts and using Wishing Pieces. Dens and beams remain visible. Y-Comm joining and Dynamax Adventures remain separate.

60FPS Opening and demos now includes evolution, post evolution, title and egg sequences. Absolute frame jump destinations scale with the sequence timeline. Recognized older output can be upgraded or removed, including cleanup when no new timing files need writing. Other cinematic timing and audio synchronization can still vary.

Gameplay Settings moves Experience Share, Experience Rate and EXP Level Cap into X > Options. Upgrading removes the recognized old PC menu components while preserving saved settings. The package also corrects the runtime mapping failure associated with the old PC entry. Gameplay Settings remains Beta.

Data Cache preparation reuses the current vanilla work plan and completed progress across ordinary editing and output refresh. Warmup continues away from Project Setup, yields to foreground operations, and avoids rebuilding the text source plan for every item.
Battle Cafe Rewards uses the shared Start Editing, Stage and Cancel workflow with an action bar that stays visible while scrolling.
Starmobile pending edits remain usable after their generated output is deleted. Apply uses the current vanilla record with the pending changes, without restoring deleted saved edits from History.
Combined Moves and Starmobile output respects the resulting move availability regardless of staging order. Invalid assignments prevent the combined write.
The 3D Model Editor better retains surface color in shaded areas under Studio and In Game lighting. This affects preview rendering, not saved materials or game lighting.

All supported physical TMs, including added TMs, can use TM numbers 1 through 201. Selecting an occupied number swaps numbering with its current owner while preserving stable item identities, taught moves and shop references. Changing only a number does not rewrite Pokemon compatibility.

An unused TM can receive a move assignment and a new number in the same staged batch. For example, assign Vine Whip to the unused TM201 slot and change it to TM161 before one Review and Apply. Compatibility editing for the newly assigned move becomes available after Apply and reload.

TM reassignment preserves existing compatibility for the selected move without creating duplicate references. Batches resolve swaps from the original assignments, support moves with no previous compatibility, and allow an added TM to use a move freed by another edit in that batch. Final duplicate TM move assignments remain invalid.

Vanilla TM restoration matches Pokemon identity and original move membership even after compatibility positions have changed. Compatibility lists can grow when necessary, and unchanged compatibility produces no Personal output.

Items and Pokemon edits can update shared generated files in successive operations without conflicting ownership claims. Standalone descriptor output includes every affected table, while Trinity Mod Manager and Trinity Bypass retain their own layouts.
Show Unused Items defaults unchecked and remembers the chosen state across output refresh, project changes and application restart.

Texture recoloring is in Textures. Materials retains material properties, tints and bindings. Selecting a material outlines its visible meshes, and selecting it again can restore that outline. Material and texture Stage and Discard controls appear at the top for the active category.

Close editor remains available during model drafting and operations. A confirmation lets you stay with your drafts or close and discard unstaged drafts; staged edits remain in Changes. Material scalar labels appear once, and Studio grid controls have clearer spacing.

Texture tolerance guidance explains that 0 percent matches the source color and 100 percent affects every visible color in the selected texture. Shared textures still affect every part that uses them.

Sound Studio recognizes supported music track references and categorizes more complete recordings under Music / BGM. Ambiguous uses remain under Other. Playback still auditions individual recordings rather than recreating interactive music events.
Scarlet, Violet and Legends Z-A require a valid user selected support folder before editors appear, alongside valid base paths. Missing support is reported in Project Setup diagnostics.

Beta Editors remain hidden until paths are validated and the Beta Editors setting is enabled. Cache status says Not checked and Awaiting path validation before validation begins, then distinguishes path validation from cache checking.

Install Update can display its confirmation and diagnostics directly in the Welcome Hub. The hub includes the 2.6.2 notes, and navigation titles for Trainer Whiteout, Trainer Dynamax and Raid Dens are available in all seven interface languages.
Application, setup, updater and window title metadata identify KM Editor 2.6.2 consistently.
The Windows release includes the custom x64 setup executable, its updater signature, the updater manifest and checksums.

summary.en: KM Editor 2.6.1 adds Sound Studio, brings the 3D Model Editor to every supported game, and introduces a dedicated Starmobiles editor for Scarlet and Violet. It also adds direct Gameplay Settings installation to emulator folders and improves trainer copying, History, diagnostics, and desktop presentation.

body.en: Sound Studio is a new tool below 3D Model Editor for Sword, Shield, Scarlet, Violet, and Legends Z-A. Browse music, cries, battle effects, interface sounds, ambience, and other discovered audio with categories and search.

Select a recording without autoplay, then use play, pause, stop, seeking, repeat, embedded loops, volume, and mute. Peak and RMS meters show the audio after app volume, with clipping indication and an optional spectrum display.

Original bank names and media identifiers remain visible, with readable names where reliable mappings exist. Unsupported recordings, procedural sounds, and unresolved references retain explanations. Playback auditions individual recordings; it does not recreate complete interactive events or layered music behavior. No game audio is bundled, and browsing does not write game output.

The 3D Model Editor is available under Tools for all five games, including supported trainer models and animations. Edit Model opens a workspace with a model viewport, Parts, Materials, Textures, and Scene controls, plus animation playback below the model.

Recolor supported textures, adjust supported material properties and texture bindings, compare Original and Edited, and restore original model assets through the normal staging and output workflow. Shared undo and redo keep related draft changes together. Saved color palettes start empty until you add colors.

Inspect parts, isolate or hide meshes, choose standard or orthographic views, and use wireframe and selection outlines. Texture inspection includes full resolution images, RGBA channels, UV overlays, zoom, pan, and PNG export. Preview overlays and reduced texture resolution do not alter exported image dimensions.

Choose Studio lighting with a movable light or an In Game preview that approximates outdoor lighting. Background colors and the Studio grid are remembered. Quarter, Half, and Full texture resolution reduce preview memory use without changing saved model or texture resolution.

Model and texture caches reuse unchanged data, refresh changed sources, and avoid uploading unchanged textures again. The catalog shows the standard loading progress bar. Optional RAM and VRAM readings remain visible beside the editor title.

Animation fixes support packed visibility, shared clips, shorter held curves, animations containing only material tracks, missing trainer motion catalogs, and the RGBA eye texture format used by Magnemite. Effects, morphs, arbitrary character assemblies, and exact game scene lighting remain limited. Geometry, skeleton, and animation authoring are not included.
Model browsing, material editing, texture recoloring, original restoration, and Sound Studio are available for both games through their own supported formats.
Trainer party members retain the correct sprite after copying and staging, including projects using another game text language.

Gameplay Settings packages include the runtime initialization correction for the added native menu functions, addressing the unresolved function calls encountered through the PC entry. Gameplay Settings remains Beta.

The new Starmobiles editor appears directly below Trainers and implements the Starmobile feature request in issue #506. Segin, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah, and Caph have named sprite selectors, a full width editing panel, and individual Reset to vanilla actions.

Edit level, fixed combat stats, HP multiplier, both types, abilities, and the three ordinary move slots. Signature moves remain locked. Speed displays the effective value set by the signature move during battle setup and is read only. Level changes do not recalculate the fixed stats; unsupported held item, EV, IV, and nature fields are omitted.

Starmobiles uses the shared Start Editing, Stage, and Cancel flow and all three output modes. Editable combat stats accept 1 through 255; level and HP multiplier accept 1 through 100. Different types occupy both type slots, while repeating a type gives one type. Empty move slots must remain at the end.

The 3D Model Editor supports the verified normal and shiny material variants. Texture and material writes preserve unrelated fields and assets, with original restoration available for the selected model.
Copied trainer party slots retain localized species names and matching sprites after staging, instead of showing internal species labels.
The 3D Model Editor supports model browsing, animation playback, material editing, texture recoloring, original restoration, and verified shiny variants through the Legends Z-A asset formats.
Sound Studio discovers supported bank and package recordings, retaining original identifiers when a reliable readable name is unavailable.

Save a Ryujinx or Eden data folder in Gameplay Settings and let KM Editor install, refresh, upgrade, or remove its package in the correct mod and SD locations. Folder checks inspect only the directories the selected operation needs. Unrelated folders and files are ignored and preserved.
The page uses a simpler target, folder, package status, and primary action layout, with technical details and file reviews available when needed. Console output keeps its export workflow.

Package inspection uses the owning backend process and its preparation budget, correcting the inspection failures reported in 2.6.0. Reviewed source and destination checks protect installation and removal. Gameplay Settings remains restricted to its supported game builds and verified Experience award paths.

Pokemon and Starmobile type changes display type names instead of numeric values. History resolves readable record names, field labels, moves, abilities, and other supported options for existing and new entries across all games.

Historical labels are presentation only. Original summaries and raw values remain in Technical Details, and older entries keep their recorded descriptions when labels cannot be resolved. Stored receipts, ownership records, review hashes, and the ability to make future changes remain intact.
Welcome Settings now shows the same gold exclamation as the game sidebar when a newer release is available. The hub includes the 2.6.1 notes and an updated developer message.

Successful Base RomFS, Base ExeFS, and Output Root identity confirmations appear only on Project Setup. Editor and game diagnostics stay out of the Welcome Hub, whose relevant diagnostics appear below its content.

Settings subsection titles and spacing are consistent. Compact headers preserve readable controls, and GPU memory totals remain available when an interface process has no graphics allocations. New editor controls and guidance are available in all seven interface languages.
Application, setup, updater, and window title metadata identify KM Editor 2.6.1 consistently.
The Windows release includes the custom x64 setup executable, its updater signature, the updater manifest, and checksums.

summary.en: KM Editor 2.6.0 adds an animated 3D Model Viewer for Scarlet and Violet, a new welcome hub, six additional themes, and app-specific RAM and VRAM diagnostics. It also expands compatibility editing, improves History and portable output support, and fixes shared output and Z-A TM batch handling.

body.en: The new welcome hub brings all five games into a persistent sidebar with saved project status, remembered game selection, release notes, and Getting started guidance. Release notes can show all games or the selected game family, always including shared app changes.

Opening a game through the hub restores its saved paths in Project Setup. Game-data loading and cache preparation wait until you press Validate Paths. You can browse the hub and choose a game without starting that work.

Settings follows the game selected in the hub. Data Cache groups the family cache controls and Analysis Loading as separate sections. Layout and Themes places layout controls above themes and appearance options below them. Language and Localization follows Updates.

The hub shows the installed app version and Made by Matroskin credit, plus a From the developer message below the notes. Documentation, GitHub, Full changelog, and Report an issue each open one browser tab. Welcome content is bundled with the app and remains available offline.

The new 3D Model Viewer under Beta Editors displays models inside the editor through DX12 with automatic graphics adapter selection. Browse Pokemon, forms, environment assets, objects, props, and other verified models, then orbit, pan, zoom, reset, or frame the view.

Animation controls include play, pause, restart, looping, play once, seeking, playback speed, and rest pose. The viewer supports skeletal animation and supported visibility, color, and texture-coordinate tracks, with layered colors and small compressed textures.

The viewer is read only: it does not edit or export models or write game output. Lighting and curve interpolation are approximate; effects, morph targets, some material channels, and complete shared character assembly remain unsupported. Missing optional animation data leaves supported geometry viewable with a warning. Enable Show Beta Editors in Settings to access it.

Output remains editable when switching between a single editor and combined editor batches. Shared descriptor and TM control updates preserve compatible ownership records, history, and checkpoints while checking the current files and each editor’s write scope.

Items now provides individual and bulk Pokemon compatibility controls for TMs. Trainer AI controls consistently handle the shared Double flag, remove the duplicate Raid choice, and correct the Weak description. TM Machine Controls sends staged policy choices through Changes for review and output.

Items now provides individual and bulk Pokemon compatibility controls for TMs and TRs. TM and TR groups keep their exact machine assignments and bit positions, including machines that teach the same move.

Advanced editors use clearer status, selection, and action areas with expandable technical details. Starting Items and Catch Cap have roomier scrollable rows, Royal Candy uses descriptive workflow cards, and Fashion Unlock and Gym Uniform Removal remove redundant explanatory tables while retaining their actions and safeguards.

Items now provides individual and bulk Pokemon compatibility controls for TMs. Batches that enable several moves correctly reserve empty slots per Pokemon and expand the personal table when needed, preserving every requested move and accompanying edit across all three output modes.

Trainer AI controls expose Basic, Strong, Expert, and Change while preserving other stored flags. Enable Change for All includes loaded trainers hidden by filters and retains its confirmation, staging, and draft safeguards.

Zero Trainer move assignments display as Not specified. The editor explains that these are stored assignments rather than a resolved battle moveset; explicit moves and zero values keep their existing storage meaning.

Pokemon compatibility groups offer Enable All, Disable All, and Restore Vanilla, including entries hidden by search. Items bulk compatibility actions follow Show all Pokemon and include entries hidden by search. Compatibility changes remain drafts until staged, Cancel discards them, and failed staging preserves the input.

Focused learnset rows, encounter slots, and Trainer party slots support Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V through the existing internal editor clipboard. Normal text editing, game compatibility checks, and context menus remain available; external clipboard text cannot become editor records.

Changes identifies staged shop removals individually, allowing one removal to be restored while keeping other removals, additions, replacements, and ordering. Duplicate items are handled by occurrence, and associated operations keep their atomic removal rules.

Workbench comparison catalogs search the complete prepared study across all five games, report complete metric counts, and load record details only when selected. Searchable paged choices retain selections, reject stale responses, and let failed reads be retried.

History has its own page between Changes and Settings. It groups transactions by local date and editor, pages transactions and recorded changes, and keeps long lists within a scrollable area. Older file-only receipts remain readable without inventing individual edit details.

Existing output stays editable after app updates and configuration changes, including relocated source or support folders. Output history, checkpoints, restore, and supported gameplay package operations remain available for the selected game and output folder.

Durable output history, ownership, checkpoints, and legacy Mod Merger metadata use separate workspaces for each exact game and output location. Verified migration preserves existing records and resumes interrupted work; unprovable conflicts stay blocked with their copies preserved.

FAT, FAT32, and exFAT output locations use protected workspace recovery journals while temporary working files stay on the output volume. Existing NTFS protections, project isolation, review checks, and pending recovery safeguards remain in place. Filesystem limits, including FAT32 single-file limits, still apply.

Six new themes join Classic, Renegade, and Royal: Sovereign, Arcane, Relic, Sword and Shield, Scarlet and Violet, and Legends Z-A. Their matching emblems and palettes extend across editor controls, tables, selections, diagnostics, and type effectiveness cells while preserving accessibility preferences.

Page headers center the selected game and align the page title with navigation and optional memory readings. The sticky Pokemon editing bar keeps the selected sprite and name visible, and advanced editor layouts provide more space for controls. Type Chart cells distinguish immunity, resistance, and weakness across themes.

Trainer item icons use a bundled catalog with dedicated sprites or representative KM category symbols. Unknown items and failed artwork keep numbered fallbacks, None stays empty, and spacing prevents item and Pokemon sprites from colliding.

Diagnostics shows private RAM, committed memory, and GPU-local VRAM for this KM Editor instance, its workers, and the interface renderer. Independent options show RAM and VRAM beside page titles, with VRAM below RAM. Unsupported readings show unavailable values; integrated graphics may count shared system memory as GPU-local memory.

Idle disposable worker caches are released sooner when system memory is tight and reload on demand. Active and queued work, session state, and source handles remain protected. Diagnostics and header readings share one sampler that pauses while hidden.

Source diagnostics retain the useful workflow explanation, severity, and recovery context while keeping technical details bounded. New controls and guidance are available in all seven interface languages, including a saved Show Beta Editors setting that defaults to off.
Successful output clears repeated pending-validation and preview messages across all five games. Warnings, errors, and current apply instructions remain visible.
Application package, Tauri, Cargo, lockfile, setup, and window title metadata identify KM Editor 2.6.0 consistently.
The Windows release contains the custom x64 setup executable, its updater signature, the updater manifest, and checksums.

summary.en: KM Editor 2.5.9 improves draft preservation, shared staging, Trainer team editing, and output reliability across the supported games. It fixes Legends Z-A Gift Review failures, expands Z-A Fashion Catalog and read-only Game Tools, and brings consistent searchable controls and keyboard navigation to more editor surfaces.

body.en: Record drafts stay associated with their owning records while users change searches, filters, categories, pages, and child selections. Retained input outside the visible row still receives draft protection.

Moving from a fully staged editor to Changes no longer asks users to revert their work. When unstaged input remains, the warning distinguishes that local draft from the staged session and preserves the staged changes after a deliberate draft discard.
Failed staging keeps the user's input available. Successful staging clears only the submitted values, so later typing or a newly selected draft is not cleared by an older completion.
Trainer categories persist while users navigate to other editors and return. Recent records remain ordered, identify the active destination, and keep scrolling inside their own rail.

Interactive editor rows support Enter and Space, compatibility lists accept keyboard focus, and tooltips and context menus expose consistent assistive relationships. Classic tables keep their first column reachable in narrow panes.

Finite option fields use KM's searchable listbox with localized choices, disabled and grouped entries, and bounded selection. Rapid search and compatibility input no longer triggers repeated intermediate state changes.
Renegade uses graphite and crimson across the remaining neutral surfaces. Primary actions retain readable hover contrast across supported themes and accessibility palettes.

One Stage Trainer Changes action submits ordinary trainer fields and party drafts retained across multiple trainers in an ordered batch. MAX IV and dedicated Z-A trainer identity actions keep their separate scope.

Copied party members remain reusable. Users can paste into consecutive empty slots without staging between each paste; a valid preceding draft counts, while genuine gaps and invalid predecessors remain blocked.
Empty species-zero party slots stay visually empty instead of displaying Egg artwork.

Shared-session validation and overlays operate on each editor's own changes while preserving other editors' work for Review and Apply. Pokemon compatibility, Items, and encounter edits no longer misinterpret unrelated pending fields.
Multi-record staging validates the complete batch and restores the original pending session on failure instead of leaving partial staged progress.

Legends Z-A Gift Pokemon now passes final Review on its own and in combined sessions. The fix preserves verified vanilla restoration and all source, output preimage, and final Apply checks in every output mode.

Failed source verification in Scarlet and Violet and Legends Z-A shows the classified reason, affected relative resource, and recovery guidance before technical details are expanded. Internal review metadata errors are distinguished from unreadable game data, with guidance in all seven interface languages.
Changes shows Needs fixes when final Review blocks output, even if earlier editor validation succeeded.
Reviewed Scarlet and Violet and Legends Z-A writes commit as one coordinated output transaction, including multi-file and deletion-only plans, with durable success or failure evidence for recovery.

Output locking and cache preparation no longer contend through conflicting lock order. Read-only analysis can continue when an optional Output Root is unavailable before observation, while Apply, recovery, active locks, and source-read failures keep their safety checks.
Long complete bridge requests return without waiting for more input. Request scheduling bounds queued work and preserves ordered state changes and output ownership.
Repeated clicks and rapid navigation no longer start contradictory duplicate operations or let stale results replace the active project, selection, or draft.
Archive-backed staging, Review, and export reuse fresh data within each operation to reduce repeated archive work. Final revalidation still reads current source data independently.

Fashion Catalog distinguishes clothing purchase price from category menu position. Category allocation and position remain read only, while supported footwear rows expose source-proven subtype choices.

Unsafe older Fashion pending edits fail safely instead of targeting newly identified fields. Existing lineup edits preserve shop identity, activation metadata, entry count, conditions, and unexposed data.
Game Tools adds read-only Static Map Markers, Named Flag and Work Catalog, and Pokemon Resource Catalog views with searchable source records and explicit coverage limits.
A missing or invalid catalog does not disable unrelated tools. These views do not edit progression, read live save values, replace models, or prove runtime visibility.
Application package, Tauri, Cargo, lockfile, setup, and window title metadata identify KM Editor 2.5.9 consistently.
The Windows release contains the custom x64 setup executable, its updater signature, the updater manifest, and checksums.

I am looking forward to seeing what you do with the expanded restoration catalog, custom gifts, and new encounter tools. Thank you for sharing your projects and helping track down issues. Come share what you are making in KM Hub!

body.en: Legends Arceus joins KM Editor, and more missing Pokemon are ready to return to Sword and Shield. I hope these new tools help you build something you are excited to play. Thank you for sharing your ideas, reporting issues, and helping KM Editor grow. Come share what you are making in KM Hub!

Ich hoffe, diese neuen Werkzeuge helfen dir, etwas zu erschaffen, das du selbst gerne spielen möchtest. Danke für deine Ideen, Fehlermeldungen und deine Unterstützung bei der Weiterentwicklung von KM Editor. Zeig uns im KM Hub, woran du arbeitest!
body.es: Legends Arceus se une a KM Editor, y más Pokémon ausentes pueden volver a Espada y Escudo. Espero que estas nuevas herramientas te ayuden a crear algo que te entusiasme jugar. Gracias por compartir tus ideas, informar de problemas y ayudar a que KM Editor siga creciendo. ¡Comparte lo que estás creando en KM Hub!
body.fr: Legends Arceus rejoint KM Editor, et davantage de Pokémon absents peuvent revenir dans Épée et Bouclier. J’espère que ces nouveaux outils vous aideront à créer une aventure à laquelle vous aurez envie de jouer. Merci de partager vos idées, de signaler les problèmes et d’aider KM Editor à évoluer. Venez nous montrer vos créations sur KM Hub !

Надеюсь, новые инструменты помогут вам создать приключение, в которое захочется играть. Спасибо за идеи, сообщения об ошибках и помощь в развитии KM Editor. Делитесь своими проектами в KM Hub!

Дякую за ідеї, повідомлення про помилки та допомогу в розвитку KM Editor. Діліться своїми проєктами в KM Hub!

body.fr: KM Editor vous aide à transformer vos idées en aventures jouables, des petits ajustements aux refontes complètes. Vos retours m’aident à l’améliorer. Merci de créer avec KM Editor !
body.ru: KM Editor помогает превратить ваши идеи в игровые приключения: от небольших изменений до полной переработки игры. Ваши отзывы помогают мне делать редактор лучше. Спасибо, что создаёте с KM Editor!

body.en: The new mod merger allows you to play with the mods you want. Merge any mods you want together to create the game you've always wanted without the headache of figuring out compatibility.
body.de: Mit dem neuen Mod Merger kannst du mit den Mods spielen, die du möchtest. Kombiniere beliebige Mods und gestalte das Spiel, das du dir schon immer gewünscht hast, ohne dir den Kopf über die Kompatibilität zerbrechen zu müssen.
body.es: El nuevo Mod Merger te permite jugar con los mods que quieras. Combina los mods que quieras para crear el juego que siempre has deseado sin el quebradero de cabeza de resolver su compatibilidad.
body.fr: Le nouveau Mod Merger vous permet de jouer avec les mods de votre choix. Fusionnez les mods que vous voulez pour créer le jeu dont vous avez toujours rêvé, sans vous casser la tête avec les questions de compatibilité.

body.uk: Новий Mod Merger дозволяє грати з тими модами, які вам подобаються. Об’єднуйте будь-які моди та створюйте гру, про яку завжди мріяли, без головного болю з перевіркою сумісності.
body.zh: 全新的模组合并器让你自由选择想玩的模组。将你想要的模组合并起来，打造一直梦寐以求的游戏，不必再为兼容性问题头疼。
